Leduc et al. 2024 - pSCoPE (Nat. Protoc.): monocyte, melanoma and PDAC cells

leduc2024_pSCoPE.Rd

Single cell proteomics data acquired by the Slavov Lab. This is an update of leduc2022_pSCoPE. The dataset contains quantitative information from three cell lines (U-937 monocyte, WM-989 Melanoma and CPAFII PDAC) at precursor, peptide and protein levels. This version of the data was acquired using the pSCoPE MS acquisition approach.

Format

A QFeatures object with 64 sets, each set being a SingleCellExperiment object:

  • Sets 1-61: log-transformed precursor-level single-cell data acquired with a 32-plex TMTpro protocol, hence these assays contain 32 columns. Columns contain quantitative information from single-cell channels, carrier channels, reference channels, empty (negative control) channels and unused channels.

  • peptides: peptide-level data containing quantitative data for 13427 peptides in 1769 single cells.

  • proteins: protein-level data aggregated based on Leading.razor.protein, containing quantitative data for 1909 proteins in 1769 single cells.

  • imported_proteins: protein-level table imported from the authors' protein report, containing 1775 proteins in 1526 single cells.

The colData(leduc2024_pSCoPE()) contains cell type annotation and batch annotation that are common to all sets.

Source

The links to the data were found on the Slavov Lab website. The data were downloaded from the Google drive folder. The raw data and quantification data can also be found in the MassIVE repository MSV000094207: ftp://massive.ucsd.edu/MSV000094207.

Acquisition protocol

The data were acquired using the following setup. More information can be found in the source article (see References).

  • Cell isolation: CellenONE cell sorting.

  • Sample preparation performed using the improved SCoPE2 protocol using the CellenONE liquid handling system: nPOP cell lysis (DMSO) + trypsin digestion + TMT-32plex labelling and pooling. The DDA data were acquired following the procedure outlined in Huffman et al. (2022). Separation: online nLC (Neo Vanquish HPLC) with a 25cm x 75um IonOpticks Aurora column (active gradient ~24 min).

  • Mass spectrometry: Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer.

  • Data analysis: MaxQuant.

Data collection

The PSM data were collected from a massIVE repository (see Source section). The archive f.MSV000094207/search/All_1p_FDR.zip contains the following file of interest:

  • evidence.txt: PSM-level quantitative data

Sample metadata were collected from a shared Google Drive folder that is accessible from the SlavovLab website (see Source section). The folder contains the following files of interest:

  • TMT_SingleCell_Meta.csv: sample-level annotations

  • TMT_ProteinxSingleCell.csv: processed protein-level data table provided by the authors, containing the imported_proteins data

We formatted sample-level annotations to ensure columns match with those of the quantification tables. Sample annotations containing NA values for neg samples were manually filled in based on the ID column in order to circumvent duplicate sample naming errors. These changes are incorporated in the file TMT_ProteinxSingleCell_modified.csv, available on Zenodo.

Both quantification and annotation tables were then combined in a single QFeatures object using QFeatures::readQFeatures().

The script to reproduce the QFeatures object is available at inst/scripts/make-data_leduc2024_pSCoPE.R.

References

Andrew Leduc, Luke Khoury, Joshua Cantlon, Saad Khan & Nikolai Slavov. 2024. “Massively parallel sample preparation for multiplexed single-cell proteomics using nPOP.” Nature Protocols 19: 3750–3776. Link to article.

Andrew Leduc, Gray Huffman, Joshua Cantlon, Saad Khan & Nikolai Slavov, 2022. “Exploring functional protein covariation across single cells using nPOP.” Genome Biology 23, 261. Link to article

Gray Huffman, Andrew Leduc, Christoph Wichmann, Marco di Gioia, Francesco Borriello, Harrison Specht, Jason Derks, et al. 2023. "Prioritized mass spectrometry increases the depth, sensitivity and data completeness of single-cell proteomics." Nature Methods 20: 714-722. Link to article
